title: 서비스 in Korea = FREE 🥟 (not "service") #learnkorean
caption:
서비스 (seo-bi-seu) = FREE — it's on the house 🥟
In a Korean restaurant, when the owner sets down something you didn't order and says 서비스~!, you don't pay for it.
Mongle didn't know… and pushed its wallet over 😅

Words in this video:
서비스 (seo-bi-seu) = something extra for free, from the shop
얼마예요? (eol-ma-ye-yo?) = How much is it?
아니 아니~ (a-ni a-ni~) = No, no~
서비스예요~ (seo-bi-seu-ye-yo~) = It's on the house~

Tip: 서비스 is the owner's gift — it's not something you ask for. Just say 감사합니다! (gam-sa-ham-ni-da = Thank you!)

pinnedComment: What did YOU get as 서비스 in Korea? 🥟👇
alt: A needle-felt miniature Korean-Chinese restaurant lit by red felt lanterns. A felt restaurant owner in a white chef's jacket and red apron sets a plate of fried dumplings in front of Mongle, a coral felt blob mascot with no arms, and says 서비스~! (Service~!). Sweating, Mongle slides its whole body forward and pushes its yellow felt wallet across the table to the owner's hand, asking 얼마예요…? (How much…?). The owner bursts out laughing, waves 'no, no' and pushes the wallet back: 아니 아니~ 서비스! A hanging price tag explains: 서비스 (seo-bi-seu) = ₩0 = FREE, on the house. Later, a tourist at the next table gets free dumplings too and holds out his wallet, and Mongle tells him 서비스예요~! (It's on the house~!).
